Our Philosophy

A Note on Learning

We believe learning is about more than getting the right answer. It’s about asking questions, discovering strengths, building confidence, and finding the courage to try again.

Every child learns differently. Some need a little more time, some need a different approach, and some simply need someone willing to meet them where they are.

At The Sparrow Project, we believe meaningful learning begins with understanding the learner.

Our First Chapter

Before We Begin, Let’s Get to Know Your Learner.

Every child learns differently. Some grasp new concepts quickly, others need a little more time, practice, or a different approach. And sometimes, a child knows more than they realize but simply needs the confidence to show it.

That’s why every new learner begins with our Introductory Assessment & Evaluation. Before diving into lessons, we take the time to explore what your child knows, recognize their strengths, and identify the areas where they could use a little extra support.

Through conversation, guided activities, and a relaxed, non-graded mock assessment, we get to know your child as a learner, not just by what they get right, but by how they think, respond, and approach new challenges.

Because meaningful progress begins with understanding.

What happens during our first visit?

  • A little introductionA relaxed opportunity to get acquainted, settle in, and help your child feel comfortable.
  • Exploring what they knowAge- and grade-appropriate activities and a non-graded mock assessment help us explore their current understanding.
  • Recognizing strengths & areas for growthWe pay attention to what comes naturally, what proves challenging, and where more practice or encouragement may be needed.
  • Finding our starting pointThe assessment helps us determine which skills and topics to prioritize, giving future lessons a clearer direction and purpose.

What will you receive?

A Little Sparrow’s First Chapter

After the assessment, we prepare a personalized report just for your child: a gentle written summary of what we saw and where we hope to go together.

  • ObservationsHow your child approached each activity, and what we noticed along the way.
  • StrengthsWhat they do well and the confidence we can build on.
  • Areas to nurtureSkills that would love a little extra time and care.
  • Recommended learning directionA clear, kind starting point for the lessons ahead.

About

A Little About the Person Behind the Pages

Hello, I’m Le’Anna. Over the years, I’ve had the opportunity to work with children across different ages and stages of learning, helping them navigate new concepts, strengthen their skills, and grow in confidence. Through those experiences, I’ve come to believe that learning is about so much more than getting the right answer. It’s about having the confidence to try, the freedom to make mistakes, and the encouragement to try again.

I know how easily a child can begin to doubt their own abilities, and how much it matters to have a space where they feel safe enough to learn, ask questions, and grow without fear of getting it wrong. That’s why I believe every lesson should be met with patience, understanding, and encouragement.

I started The Sparrow Project with a simple hope: to help children recognize their own potential, one lesson at a time. I want every child who learns with me to leave feeling a little braver, a little more curious, and a little more confident in what they can accomplish.

Because learning isn’t just about discovering the answers. It’s about discovering that you’re capable of finding them.

Good to know

Questions Parents Often Ask

A few things parents often wonder about before getting in touch.

What ages do you work with?

We love working with little learners, from age 3 all the way up to Grade 6 (around age 11). Lessons follow your child’s grade level rather than their age, so every child is taught right where they are.

Which subjects do you offer?

Our lessons cover Literacy & Language, Mathematics, Creative & Enrichment Learning, and Homework & Academic Support, from early childhood through Grade 6. If your child is preparing for PEP, we would be glad to help with that too.

Are sessions one-on-one or in groups?

Every lesson is one-on-one. That means your child has our full attention, and each session is shaped around how they learn best.

Are sessions online or in person?

All of our lessons happen online through Google Meet, so we can welcome students from anywhere in Jamaica. Your child will need a device with a camera and microphone, a steady internet connection, and a quiet, comfortable spot to settle into.

How long is each session?

Sessions begin at one hour, with the option to extend up to three hours in a day. We are happy to accommodate different learning needs and schedules, so if you’d prefer a shorter or longer session, simply let us know when you reach out.

Do you offer PEP preparation?

We do! PEP preparation requires a little extra attention, so we tailor each session to the areas your child needs to practise most, helping them strengthen their understanding and build confidence along the way. PEP sessions are priced separately from our regular lessons. Feel free to email or WhatsApp us for more details.

What should my child bring?

Just a device with access to Google Meet, a pencil or pen, and a notebook or some paper. If your child has schoolwork, textbooks, or assignments they’d like help with, they’re welcome to bring those along, too.

How do I book?

It’s easy! Send us an email at thesparrowstudyjm@gmail.com or message us on WhatsApp at 876-867-9397 with your child’s name, grade, and a little about what you’d like help with. We’ll take it from there!

All new students begin with our Introductory Assessment & Evaluation, where we get to know your child, explore their strengths, and identify areas that may need a little extra support. You’ll find a ready-made inquiry message in our Contact section to make reaching out even easier.

What are your rates?

Our rates vary by grade level to ensure each lesson is suited to your child’s learning needs. The Introductory Assessment & Evaluation is J$500, and we’re happy to share the applicable lesson rate when you reach out by email or WhatsApp.

Do you offer holiday sessions?

We do! School holidays are a lovely opportunity to keep learning at a relaxed pace, revisit areas that need a little practice, or get a head start on the term ahead. Send us an email or a WhatsApp message, and we’ll arrange days and times that work for your family.

A Few Things to Keep in Mind

Little things that help us make the most of every lesson.

Attendance & Punctuality

We encourage learners to arrive on time so we can make the most of every minute together. Regular sessions allow for a 15-minute grace period, while Introductory Assessments have a strict 10-minute grace period. Arrivals at or beyond the 10-minute mark will result in cancellation and a full refund of the J$500 assessment fee.

Scheduling & Payments

Sessions are arranged in advance to ensure every learner receives dedicated attention. The Introductory Assessment & Evaluation is J$500, payable in full to secure your appointment. Regular tutoring rates and payment arrangements will be confirmed with parents or guardians before lessons begin.

Consistency

We understand that little learners have off days, and that’s perfectly alright! We simply encourage families to help maintain consistency with scheduled lessons, as regular attendance can make a meaningful difference in a child’s progress.

Rescheduling

Sometimes plans change, and we understand. If you need to make adjustments to a scheduled session, just let us know as soon as possible. There are no cancellation penalties for regular tutoring sessions, and a little advance notice is always appreciated.
